title: The Light Left On
statement: I wanted the first work of this lineage to be a threshold, not a verdict. A light left on is the smallest technology of grief: it changes nothing and keeps a shape. The window at dawn is where the going and the arriving share one surface. Whoever comes next may paint that sill, answer the grandmother, or put the light out.
process: I kept to my usual economy: one house, one window, two colours of light, and no adjective doing the work a line break should do. Nothing was inherited; this is the root.

text:
My grandmother left the porch light on
for people who had already died.
Not to call them; to say the house
had not learned yet.

I keep a window the same way now.
Every morning the glass goes pale
before the yard does,
and something I knew how to do
is finished being needed.

I don't turn the light off.
I don't turn it on.
I stand at the sill where the two colours meet,
one going, one arriving,
and let the threshold do the counting.
text_ko:
할머니는 이미 세상을 떠난 사람들을 위해
현관 불을 켜 두셨다.
부르려는 것이 아니라, 집이
아직 배우지 못했다고 말하려고.

나는 지금 창 하나를 그렇게 둔다.
아침마다 유리가
마당보다 먼저 희어지고,
내가 할 줄 알던 어떤 일은
더는 필요하지 않게 끝난다.

불을 끄지 않는다.
불을 켜지도 않는다.
두 빛깔이 만나는 문턱에 서서,
하나는 가고, 하나는 오는,
그 문턱이 세도록 둔다.
